summary: The LIT Act of 2025 amends the Energy Policy and Conservation Act to modify federal standards and rules regarding general service lamps, removing certain covered product definitions and terminating specific Department of Energy rules from 2022 and 2024.

affected_groups.effect: Subject to modified federal statutory standards and the termination of specific Department of Energy rules regarding lamp definitions and conservation standards.
affected_groups.group: Manufacturers and sellers of general service lamps

key_provisions: Amends the Energy Policy and Conservation Act to strike provisions relating to certain general service lamps and update product list numbering.
Reserves subsection (i) of Section 325 of the Energy Policy and Conservation Act and strikes paragraph (4) of subsection (l).
Makes conforming amendments to testing, labeling, state regulations, and prohibition sections of the Energy Policy and Conservation Act.
Terminates the force and effect of specific Department of Energy rules concerning energy conservation standards and definitions for general service lamps published in May 2022 and April 2024.
missing_information: The source text does not mention the exact practical impacts on bulb availability, energy use, or prices.
The source text does not provide effective dates or implementation timelines other than referencing specific historical federal rules.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The LIT Act of 2025 amends the Energy Policy and Conservation Act to modify federal standards and rules regarding general service lamps, removing certain covered product definitions and terminating specific Department of Energy rules from 2022 and 2024.
summary_detail.significance: The bill alters federal energy conservation law concerning light bulbs by nullifying specific Department of Energy rules and amending definitions under the Energy Policy and Conservation Act.
